# Router doc test anchors

Created in P1 of the router context cut. Every test that reads the runtime router text (`skills/craftflow-router/SKILL.md`, `skills/_shared/router-protocol.md`, `skills/craftflow-router/references/*.md`) is classified here, so a later phase that moves prose knows which assertions it has to keep true or retarget.

Kinds:

- **C (content presence).** Reads the joined router corpus (`craftflow_router_corpus`), so the text may live in any runtime router file. Retargeted in P1; a phase that moves text needs no test edit. Owning phase `none`.
- **K (kernel structure or order).** Pins where a section sits, which file holds a pointer, or an order between two sections. Stays on the files it names. The owning phase is the phase that moves one of those sections and must retarget or extend the test in that same phase. `never-move` means no planned phase moves the pinned text (the test is expected to keep passing unchanged).
- **F (file-specific counts or presence).** Asserts a property of one named file (a per-file count, a table in one reference). A corpus-wide read would make it vacuous, so it stays file-specific. Same owning-phase rule as K.

`TBD-by-mover` means the plan does not say where the asserted text ends up; the phase that moves it assigns the retarget.

Heading-uniqueness invariant (router decision, P1 REM-FIX 4). Every markdown heading text (normalized, `#` level ignored) occurs exactly once across the runtime corpus (`skills/craftflow-router/SKILL.md`, `skills/craftflow-router/references/*.md` one level deep and `skills/_shared/*.md`; nothing deeper, and no other directory). A relocation phase that keeps a pointer or trigger for a moved section writes it as a plain or bold line, not as a heading with the moved text; a file that receives a moved body has an H1 and section headings that differ from the kernel's. This is what makes a no-hint `_router_section_or_none` read location-agnostic, so the C rows stay C. It is enforced two ways: `test_router_test_anchors.py` fails on any heading that repeats beyond `HEADING_DUP_ALLOWLIST` (the pre-existing duplicates, frozen at the P1 HEAD with the phase expected to remove each; the list must match the live corpus exactly, so a phase that removes a duplicate deletes its entry), and `router_relocation_drills.py` checks every drilled copy and rejects a drill that creates a duplicate before running any suite.

Relocation drills (`router_relocation_drills.py`, run by `test_router_relocation_drills.py`): no drill remains (the P8, P9, P10 and P11 drills retired when those phases moved their sections for real; the hook-policy move did not happen because Difference 17 was dropped), so only the control run and the self-tests are left. A drill passes when every test that fails in it (and passed on the control copy, and is not a wall-clock budget test in `DRILL_IGNORED_TESTS`) is a K/F row whose owner names the drill's phase. Limits: drills are single moves on the P1 tree, never cumulative; the harness decides ownership only for moves it runs. The enumerator also misses the sibling-module constant style (`import test_rule_inventory_doubt as d; K = d.K`, used by `test_rule_inventory_doubt3.py` b1-b4 and `test_rule_inventory_rows2.py::test_rh1_e2e`); those rows are hand-added, and deleting one is not detected by the coverage guard.

Excluded tests. `tests/fixtures/router_test_enumerate.py` flags a test when its source (or a same-file helper it uses) names a router path, a corpus helper or any `SKILL.md`, so it also flags tests that mention a path without asserting runtime router prose. Each such test is excluded by exactly one line of the form `Not listed: <label>::<test> — <reason>` below. The label is `hook` or `fx::<file>`, the reason is mandatory, and a bare test name classifies nothing, so an exclusion cannot match a same-named test in another file. Of the P0 tooling fixtures, `test_router_xrefs.py` is enumerated only for the tests that read the real tree (`PLUGIN_ROOT`), and `test_rule_inventory*.py` is enumerated like every other fixture: its end-to-end tests copy or open the live router at run time and are rows below (owner: every relocation phase), the synthetic ones are excluded by the lines here. The enumerator cannot see an end-to-end test whose helper opens the router through a computed path; those rows (`test_diff_zero_unmapped`, `test_baseline_matches_ref`, `test_b1_*`, `test_b2_*`, `test_b3_*`, `test_b4_after_*`, `test_rh1_e2e_*`) are hand-classified and checked only for existing.

Failure messages of the corpus-wide tests still say "SKILL.md missing ..." because rewording `fail(name, ...)` lines would break the P1 assertion-count proof; the Kind column, not the message, says what a test reads.

Reproduce the enumeration with `python3 tests/fixtures/router_test_enumerate.py [--names]`; `tests/fixtures/test_router_test_anchors.py` fails when a router-reading test is neither a row below nor a qualified, reasoned `Not listed` line, when a row or exclusion names a test that no longer exists (stale), or when the row count line is stale.

Limits of the guard (a convention check for the in-repo style, not a proof). The enumerator reads each test's own source and the same-file helpers and constants it uses (`=`, annotated and augmented assignments, class `test_` methods), and it treats names bound by an import of the corpus loader (`import craftflow_router_corpus as rc`, `from craftflow_router_corpus import read_corpus as rd`) as router-reading, so an aliased `rc.read_corpus(...)` is seen. It does not follow a helper imported from a module that hides the loader behind its own name, a router file reached by a glob or a computed path with no marker and no loader import in the test, or a nested or dynamically built test. `fx::test_agent_structure.py` runs its checks at module level without `def test_`, so its rows below are hand-classified, are verified only by their `[section]` label still existing in the file, and a new check added there is not detected; `tests/live/*` is outside the enumeration. The enumeration skips only the exact filenames in `EXCLUDED_FILES` (the guard itself), so a new fixture is enumerated unless it is added to that list. The relocation drills (`tests/fixtures/router_relocation_drills.py`, run by `test_router_relocation_drills.py`) are the dynamic check on these rows: they apply the plan's P8/P9/P10/P11 moves on scratch copies and fail when a C row, an unclassified test or a K/F row whose owner does not name the drill's phase breaks. A SyntaxError in any `tests/fixtures/test_*.py` aborts the guard with a traceback (exit 1, no `Results:` line). `_router_section_or_none` failures report an ambiguous heading as not found or not bounded; the message wording is left as is because rewording `fail(name, ...)` lines would break the P1 assertion-count proof.

P1 test-net limits (P1 REM-FIX 5; also recorded in ADR-0073, section "P1 test-net limits"). The net is a convention check plus single-move drills, not a proof. Known holes, none fixed in P1:

1. Negative-check scope loss (exit-0 class). A `not in` check bounded to a section stops covering text that a later phase moves out of that section. Demo: `test_memory_load_anchored_to_project_root` against the 5a move (injecting `Read(".craftflow/state/project/activeContext.md")` into `memory-load-workspace.md` passes; the same injection at HEAD fails). The drills look only for failures and cannot see this. Control: the relocation phase's signed policy-map row and the reviewer must re-read every negative assertion over the moved text; P10 (the 5a mover) re-scoped that test's negative checks to the new file (done: `test_memory_load_anchored_to_project_root` now also reads `memory-load-workspace.md`).
2. Drill coverage. Drills are single moves on the current tree, never cumulative, and P12 has no drill. P10 made its moves for real and retired its seven drills; every test that failed on the real move was already a K/F row owned by P10 (the hook tests, `test_agent_structure.py`, `test_router_policy_prose.py`, `test_router_xrefs.py`, the budget and read-set tests) and is retargeted. P11 made its moves for real (protocol split into three `_shared` files, the build split, the bake-off body, the Cursor pointers) and retired its three drills; every test that failed on those moves was already a K/F row owned by P11 and is retargeted. No drill is left for P12.
3. Control-failing rows are never exercised by drills: the git and lock end-to-end rows (including the hand rows `test_b1_*`, `test_b2_*`, `test_b4_after_*` and `test_rh1_e2e_*`) and `test_craftflow_cursor_exempt_wiring.py`, which crashes on control copies (the scratch copy is not a git checkout). The exclusion reason for that file is owner P11 (P11 edits the cursor-router pointers), not "no phase moves it".
4. The heading allowlist freezes counts, not files. The corpus is `SKILL.md`, `references/*.md` one level deep and `_shared/*.md` (not `skills/craftflow-router/**`). A prose mention of a heading's text (for example § 14 citing "## 13.") hijacks a first-occurrence slice; REM-FIX 5 moved the last five raw `find("<heading>")` readers to the section helpers, and the invariant is not extended to prose, so a new raw `find` of heading text reintroduces the hole.
5. Pre-existing vacuity (not P1). `test_craftflow_router_documents_state_read_compaction_self_heal` has markers that also occur at SKILL.md:88-94; the P0 rule-inventory gate covers it.
6. The enumerator misses sibling-module constants, subprocess and rglob reads and class-attribute reads, and the drills are not cumulative (both already stated above).
